comment: I have mixed feelings: hated the course the whole semester, but ended with a 99% so... As a good student, I found the work to be relatively easy, but the professor to be condescending and out of touch. She frequently got upset about students not being able to find the homework that she hadn't mentioned, and about her own late work policy

AVOID! Only take this class if you're fluent & can think on your feet. Assignments are hard to find, with unclear instructions & due dates. Participation is 40% of your grade & she will give bad grades! Not very understanding of your personal life/other situations and thinks this class is all you've got going on. Overall, unrealistic expectations.

She is nice overall and the class was interesting. Weekly participation grades and she will give bad ones. Grading on essays and presentations seems arbitrary at times. She is disorganized and sometimes she got upset when people didn't do homework that was hard to find on Blackboard. Must be able to speak on your feet in Spanish. Note-took 307.
A big time commitment, around 30 mins of homework every night, tests are hard, need to participate in class, drill is chill

Dr. Vazquez is hard but fair. I never felt that I was robbed of a good grade. For her 221, you have to consistently focused as she cold calls, and nearly every Thursday there is a quiz. Her lectures can sometimes be boring when she covers grammar.

She was extremely helpful for this course! She helped me find a community partner that would be good for me and really understood what I was looking for. This course was perfect for me as I am both a LAIS minor and premed.

Participation was 40% of the grade, so you had to talk a lot in class to get a 9 or 10 out of 10. However, it forced me to spend a lot of time practicing Spanish outside of class even though we didn't have tests or quizzes. The Spanish-speaking volunteer part was fulfilling. Mine was 2 hours a week and she routinely offered more. My favorite class.

Dr. Vazquez is a super nice woman, however her English is not the best and her lectures are hard to follow and get off topic. We had pretty long readings for her House Keeping Inequalities class, but we had few papers to write. However, I would say she is an easy grader in general. The topic was interesting, it just got repetitive at the end.

Just absolutely amazing. She is amazing at teaching the language and wants you to do well in her class. Sometimes things can get a bit misconstrued, but ask her to clear it up in English and things fall into place. There is a solid amount of homework, but it is manageable.

I took Dr. Vazquez for HouseKeeping Inequalities. For homework expect at least 40 pages or a movie/documentary. This semester with masks she was difficult to understand during lectures, but a super nice woman! Her grading on papers is weird but not difficult to at least get a B on them.

Mediocre professor at best. You can get a good grade in this class as long as you orally participate every day. She gives extensive homework every night that is basically unnecessary. Get ready to work

Love this woman. Take her class if you can. The work is totally manageable and fair... She is beyond understanding and wants nothing more than for you to enjoy class and really absorb the material. And be happy! She is so caring and genuine. If you think anything she's saying to you is mean you should probably retake LAIS 200 and study vocab lol

Avoid this professor if you can. Class is way too hard. It is not worth it. Assigns lots of work. You have to volunteer 3 hours a week (Mon-Fri) between 9 and 5 pm. If it doesn't fit your schedule, your grade will be docked.

Hands down one of the worst classes I have taken. Prof Vazquez gives an insane amount of homework. About 25 - 30 pages of reading, 1 -3 videos, and 10-20 response questions per day. Clearly thinks her class is more important than others. If you speak in English in class she will yell at you. I took Spanish in the Community & Cooking, it was awful

There's a lot of work for this class, but you learn a whole lot. If you're planning to go abroad, you definitely want to take her class before you go. She's super helpful and you'll learn a lot of Spanish from her. She's incredibly kind and very caring, and you can tell how passionate she is about the language and about her students.

Sra. Vazquez was an amazing professor. I took Spanish in the Community, and really enjoyed it. Part of the class involved volunteering in the community each week, which was what made the class really worth it for me. At times class was repetitive or felt slow, but it was easy to find opportunities to participate. This class was very eye-opening!

I love this woman! She is so sweet and cares a lot about her students. The material was pretty easy but her tests are very long and it is very difficult to finish them during the class period. You will have homework every night, about 30 minutes to an hours worth from the text book. Also, I can't emphasize enough how many pop quizzes there are

I took Sra. Vazquez for Spanish in the community. She was a kind and passionate teacher, and loved to see students putting effort into their work with la comunidad. Homework is reading heavy, and class discussions heavily rely on the readings. You can skip the hw without consequence, but it will be reflected in your participation grade.

Sra. Vazquez is so amazing. I had her this year for Spanish in the Community and had an incredible experience. It is obvious how much she cares about what she is doing and how is resonates with the students. The class was structured essentially as a group discussion led mostly by the students and every day was something interesting. Love that woman
